title: Create and reuse a component
summary: Turn a button into a component and update every copy at once.

steps.say: Select the button frame you made, the one around your text, in the layers list.

check.prompt: Is the auto layout button frame selected?

hints: Its row in the layers list has an auto layout icon.
Finish the auto layout lesson first if you have no button yet.
steps.why: Components start from an existing design.

steps.say: Press Control Alt K to turn it into a component.

checks.prompt: Does the selected layer now show a component icon, four diamonds, in the layers list?

hints: The toolbar shows a Create component button while the frame is selected.
Right-click the layer and choose Create component.
steps.why: A component is a reusable main design.

steps.say: Double-click its name in the layers list and type Button.

check.prompt: Is there a component named Button in the layers list?

hints: Control R renames the selected layer too.
Press Enter to confirm the name.
steps.why: The name is how you find the component in Assets.

steps.say: Click the Assets tab at the top of the left sidebar.

check.prompt: Is the Assets tab open in the left sidebar, showing a Button component?

hints: It sits next to the File tab.
Use the search box in Assets if the list is long.
steps.why: Assets lists every component you can reuse.

steps.say: Drag Button from Assets onto the canvas.

check.prompt: Is there a second copy of the button on the canvas, shown with a hollow diamond instance icon?

hints: Drop it anywhere on the canvas, inside or outside a frame.
Holding Alt while you drag the original button also makes a copy.
steps.why: Each copy is an instance that follows the main component.

steps.say: Select the original Button and change its fill color.

check.prompt: Did the fill color change on both the original button and its copy?

hints: The original has the solid four-diamond icon.
Change the color under Fill in the right sidebar.
steps.why: Editing the main component updates every instance at once.
